Impermanent loss is how much your L.P. position lags simply holding the same starting tokens, once their relative price has changed. It isn't measured against zero. It's measured against the specific alternative of never having deposited at all.

beats.vo: Here's exactly why the name includes “impermanent.” The gap between your L.P. position and simply holding only becomes a real, locked-in loss the moment you withdraw. If the price ratio moves back to where it started before you withdraw, that gap closes completely, back to zero. Withdraw while the ratio is still different from your entry, and what was impermanent becomes permanent, instantly.
